risks.title: Technological obsolescence and loss of competitiveness
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned first in the risk factors summary, the language is strong ('obsolete', 'less competitive'). The context is rapid IT market evolution. Weighting is high as technology is core to the business.

risks.title: Intense competition and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: The market is described as 'highly competitive' and 'evolving rapidly'. Risk of 'commoditization' and price reduction is explicitly mentioned. Competition is a key factor in the technology sector.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and security breaches
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed with high intensity ('significantly harm', 'material adverse effect') and amplified by geopolitical context ('geopolitical conflicts'). Dependence on platform and data makes this an existential risk.

risks.title: Dependence on partner platforms and integrations
risks.score_rationale: The text highlights dependence on 'demand- and supply-side advertising platforms' and 'social platforms'. These partners may develop competing products or control access, negatively impacting revenues.

risks.title: Risks related to artificial intelligence and machine learning
risks.score_rationale: Specifically mentioned ('risks associated with our use of artificial intelligence and machine learning models') and linked to technological evolution and cybersecurity. AI is a key technology but carries uncertainties regarding effectiveness and security.

risks.title: Regulation on privacy and digital advertising
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned ('Data privacy legislation and regulation', 'Public criticism of digital advertising'). Regulatory changes and public perception can directly impact the business model.

risks.title: Dependence on key personnel and recruitment
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions dependence on the management team and key personnel ('depend on our management team and other key personnel'). Loss of such talent or inability to recruit new talent is an identified risk.

ai_positioning.summary: DoubleVerify positions AI at the core of its strategy. The company explicitly describes its offering as a media effectiveness measurement platform using AI to optimize brand outcomes. AI is cited as a key factor in addressing the rapidly evolving internet and in developing media quality protection and strategic campaign alignment solutions.
evidence: Official tagline: 'leverages artificial intelligence (AI) to drive superior outcomes for global brands'
Artificial Intelligence section in the MDA: 'The rapidly-evolving, AI-powered internet will amplify advertisers need to protect media quality and we intend to continue to develop solutions'
Identified risks related to AI: 'risks associated with our use of artificial intelligence and machine learning models'
